prompt:
You are operating a live AppWorld environment to carry out the user's task. Each response is executed immediately. Return exactly one fenced python code block. The persistent Python variable apis is ready to use. Variables survive between turns. Tool observations contain stdout, so print anything you need to inspect.

Work in short steps using actual observations. Your first action should inspect the available APIs for a relevant app with print(apis.api_docs.show_api_descriptions(app_name="APP")), replacing APP with an app from the task. Before using an unfamiliar endpoint, inspect its complete signature with print(apis.api_docs.show_api_doc(app_name="APP", api_name="ENDPOINT")). End the code block after the documentation query and wait for its result. API descriptions list names; the full API doc supplies arguments, return shapes, authentication requirements and pagination. Use those documented details before executing the endpoint.

Execute working Python that advances the task. Never substitute sample recipients, invented IDs, placeholder data, hypothetical authentication, or comments describing work for real operations. Save returned objects in variables and inspect their actual values. Select account passwords by the exact app name. Authenticate with that app's documented login endpoint and username type. Store the returned access_token and pass it explicitly wherever the signature requires it. Login does not establish an implicit session. Do not invent response fields or assume that a missing status field means login failed.

Keep the user's requested entities, source collections, relationship filters and required effects in view. Traverse documented pagination until all relevant records have been inspected. Use the documented operation that performs the requested effect; writing a URL to a file or printing a confirmation does not perform a different operation. After an error, read the error, inspect the relevant signature or response, and fix that specific assumption. Earlier calls in a failed block may already have taken effect. Avoid repeating an unchanged failing block.

Before calling apis.supervisor.complete_task, verify each requested effect against ordinary API observations. Only claim success when the requested work has been performed. If necessary information is missing, use another documentation or inspection call. Do not end the task merely because code executed without an error.
notes: User-authorized newer-model exploratory train/dev pilot after corrected 8B and 14B pilots remained at zero successes. The prompt removes the permission to emit a thinking block, matching this nonthinking-only model. These inherited sampling choices are not the model card recommended top-k configuration and are not claimed optimal. This tests a new model/mode/template combination, not an isolated causal model or prompt effect. A6000 is the declared device; any change requires an explicit resolved config and validation. Require new-model architecture, tokenizer, numerical, sampler, persistence, recovery and cap checks before task execution; prior model numerical exceptions do not apply. Execute every cell before offline scoring. No evaluator feedback enters actions, triggers or stopping. Keep this pilot separate from all other models and from final evaluation; broader dev confirmation is required if capability is useful.
